title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The idea in the background is to use a simplicial object of PD polynomial differential forms on the standard simplices, A_h = (A^*_{h,n})_n, as an integral or mod-p analogue of Sullivan's ∇(n,*). The functor X ↦ Hom(X_•, A^*_{h,•}) then sends simplicial sets to commutative DG algebras. The index h is probably a truncation or level parameter of the PD forms, but it is unclear.

What the page says:
(1) The previous discussion seems to have shown that, apart from the operations already present on the cohomology of such complexes (the transcription reads "opérations de Ω …", possibly divided powers or de Rham-type operations), nothing new appears automatically. To get interesting cohomology operations one must first work in characteristic 2 (or p). There one may hope to describe the Steenrod squares 'und so' through this formalism, which is flagged as something to check.
(2) A 'more clever' alternative is proposed. Apply a functor τ_ω: M → M^w, where M is perhaps the category of graded modules or sheaves ("Mod gr.d Sh"). M^w is described as an abelian category 'of characteristic …' with a commutative tensor product. Composing gives a functor (simplicial sets) → (DG algebras in M^w), X ↦ Hom(X_•, A^*_{h,•}).
(3) Then forget the grading and keep only the structure of differential ring. Compute the automorphism group of this functor, first for fixed h and then how it varies with h. The hope is to find cohomology operations other than the Steenrod powers.

This is a Tannakian or 'Galois group of a fibre functor' approach to cohomology operations. The operations would be recovered as symmetries of a strictly commutative cochain-algebra functor. A marginal 'Non' with an arrow pointing at the final sentence shows Grothendieck later rejected the hope, or perhaps the whole approach.
errors: No proof is given; the page is a heuristic plan. The marginal 'Non' indicates Grothendieck himself judged the final expectation (new operations beyond the Steenrod powers) to be wrong.

Strictly commutative functorial cochain models cannot carry the full mod-p homotopy information: Steenrod operations are an obstruction to commutativity. So automorphisms of a strictly commutative PD model are unlikely to yield operations beyond the Steenrod algebra. Natural stable operations on mod-p cohomology are exactly the Steenrod algebra, so 'new' operations would have to be unstable or non-additive, or live in a different theory.

ideas.what: Commutative cochain functor on simplicial sets via simplicial PD polynomial de Rham forms, X ↦ Hom(X_•, A^*_•)
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan polynomial forms A_PL; integral/divided-power variants (Cartan, 'Théories cohomologiques')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), Cartan (1976); PD variants discussed by Cartan and others

ideas.what: Recover cohomology operations as the automorphism group of the cochain-algebra functor, i.e. the 'Galois group' of a fibre functor
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian / representability viewpoint on operations; endomorphisms of cochain functors (cf. Mandell's E∞-cochain theorems, the Steenrod algebra as natural operations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod/Serre/Cartan (operations); Mandell (2001, 2006) for E∞ cochains determining homotopy type
ideas.where_published: Possibly loosely echoed in Pursuing Stacks discussions of cochain models; unsure

ideas.what: Expectation that Steenrod squares arise from the PD de Rham formalism in characteristic 2
ideas.modern_name: Steenrod operations via divided powers / cup-i structure on commutative-up-to-homotopy cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod; May ('A general algebraic approach to Steenrod operations', 1970)

missed.claim: Proposal to compute the automorphism group of the functor X ↦ Hom(X_•, A^*_{h,•}) (as a DG-ring-valued functor, grading forgotten) and its variation in the parameter h, in order to find new cohomology operations. Grothendieck himself marked it 'Non'.
missed.quote: de déterminer les groupes des automorphismes de ce foncteur (d'abord pour h fixé, puis sa variation avec h). Peut-être trouverons nous des op. coh. intéressantes hors puiss. de Steenrod
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a fibre-functor viewpoint on cohomology operations that anticipates later automorphism and endomorphism computations for cochain functors (Mandell-type results, Tannakian approaches to homotopy types). Since it was self-rejected and the conclusion is essentially expected, its novelty is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: A brief, self-rejected heuristic: it recasts cohomology operations as automorphisms of a commutative PD cochain functor. It is historically interesting as a Tannakian-flavoured instinct, but contains no result and the expected outcome (nothing beyond Steenrod) is standard.
transcription_corrections: The page image is poorly legible; the reading 'Hom(X_α, A_{hα}^α)' is better read as 'Hom(X_•, A^•_{h•})' (cochains with values in a simplicial DG algebra A_h).
The parenthetical '(en caractéristique [?])' after 'car. 2' is uncertain; the phrase reads like '(en car. 2 …)' with an unclear alternative.
The arrow in the functor reads 'M → M^w' (maybe M^ω); the parenthetical before it reads roughly '(Mod gr.d Sh ⟹)'.
'oubliant' is likely correct: 'en oubliant la structure graduée au profit de la structure d'anneau diff. sans plus'.
'des op. coh. intéressantes hors puiss. de Steenrod' fits the image; the marginal 'Non' with an arrow points to these final lines.
